text:
maria: repro'd a p99 tail spike on canary this morning during a 3x burst run. digging in now.

anil: which kernel path landed? fp16 fused or int8-quant path?

maria: kernel picker favoured fused-attn-v2 for the seq profiles. interestingly, microbatching jumped from 8->32 in the same window and kvcache hit-rate dropped.

jake: saw that in the night run too. perf trace shows memcpy stalls around the kvcache invalidation point (~1.2ms gaps).

maria: uploaded trace + flame: https://redwood.s3/trace/canary/2156789012/trace.png 

sara: if batching grew that much, tail amplification is expected. p95 improved but p99 got worse, right?

maria: exactly. p95 down ~12ms, p99 up ~45ms. throughput unchanged.

mike: curious if the kernel itself has a long tail on warp-sync for odd sequence lengths. we saw that with attn-v2 on 2048 tokens.

anil: two quick knobs: force kernel hint to attn-v1 for the canary to test kernel effect, and try microbatch cap at 16. also consider soft-admit at 0.7 util instead of 0.85.

maria: test plan: A/B -- (1) kernel hint v1 vs v2, (2) microbatch max [8,16,32], (3) admission soft thresholds [0.65,0.75,0.85], measure p95/p99 + tokens/sec. I'll run 30m each under the synthetic tail generator.

jake: i'll script the runner and add a KV prefetch flag toggle. prefetch async helped us last quarter.

mike: small repro of the kernel hint change (add to runtime config):
```
serve.runtime.kernel_hint: attn_v1
serve.runtime.microbatch.max_inflight: 16
serve.runtime.admission.soft_target_util: 0.75
```

anil: if v2 still has p99 issues with smaller microbatches, then it's likely a memory-copy or kvcache eviction pattern rather than kernel compute. check CUDA stream synchronization points in the trace.

perf-bot: scheduled loadtest run_id=lt-20260318-09, variants=6, ETA=2h :gear:

maria: thanks. i'll post the results and a short table of p50/p95/p99 + tokens/s. hope we can avoid shedding but if p99 stays bad we should consider temporary shed rules for long seqs.

sara: agree — prefer graceful shed per-route for ultra-long sequences rather than global hard shed.

jake: noted, i'll include per-route admission toggles in the runner.

maria: filing a quick ticket to track: PERF-rt-2156 with links to trace and config. will update after tests. :white_check_mark:
